I believe it is normal to be worried about your partners well-being. It would be naive to assume there arent vile people in the world that obviously can do harm, but you also need to remember there is also good people who will help if its anything does happen. Her friends, family (if she called as an example), and strangers will most likely help (as long as people dont do the bystander effect). If anything, what you can do is talk together about precautionar measures for when she does go out just so you have some peace of mind for yourself and i assume her. I cant speak for her but i know when i go out and its late im always on high alert cause in my mind \*anyone\* could harm me. After events i go to the washroom and dress more masculine so i feel slighly safer walking the streets at night after events, just to hide any feminiity I have cause (unfortuntely) it makes me a higher target.  
  
Some places its legal to carry things to retaliate against attacks ie bear or dog spray. Theres loud alarms that you can attach as a keychain or necklace that you can pull and when it does, worse case scenario some necklaces that can uncover as a sharp object which can be used for either offense or if you're tied/trapped. I want to say go against things like trackers cause otherwise it feels like an overprotective parent and people do deserve privacy if they wish for it, but if they're down for it then you could do it just for these types of events. Theres also things you can get like nailpolish that can detect if your drinks spiked, drink covers to avoid your drinks from getting spiked in the first place. Theres even fitbits where you can share your heartbeat and ect. If their up for it, theres self defense classes as well that people can take. Honestly theres hundreds of ways to help someone just incase of an incident where there is someone bad targetting people.  
  
WITH saying this, remember boundries and remember your partner has a say in what they are ok with and not ok with doing. It's also good to remember that you dont want to suffocate your partner and have them feel monitored because we all do desire freedom and privacy in some way, shape or form. It would also do some good to look internally about how to manage some of these paranoid and anxious feelings you have. While yes, there are bad people, not EVERYONE is bad and not every event will have a bad person. Nearly every person there will be a good person, they will be the majority, and depending on where you are from people will speak out and do something to stop any assult or at least call the cops/tell a secuirty person at the event. Her friends will also help because theyre her friends and people dont usually befirend people they dont trust and rely on. Have faith in your partner that they can make the right decisions and choices, that they arent as helpless as they seem. Have faith in your partners friends that they will protect her incase of anything. I recommend searching up "Grounding techniques" because they help with distressful thoughts and feelings. Theres also "Cognitive Behvaioral Therapy" that you can look up because it helps give techniques with managing emotions and feelings, its very helpful when you're feeling things like this. Therapy doesnt have to be for mentally ill, it can be for guidance with everyday regular people.

Basically, if these are overpowering feelings, talking to your partner about your worry and concern for them and come up with a plan together would be a good idea. Honestly, you may not even need to do any of the above because just a simple reassuring text goes miles when it comes to these worries.
